title: Romans Road
description: A pathway through the book of Romans that explains sin, salvation, and how to receive eternal life.

cards.heading: All have sinned and fall short of God's glory
cards.scriptureText: For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
cards.body: The Romans Road begins with an honest look at our condition before God. Every person — regardless of background, morality, or religion — has sinned. Sin is not just doing bad things; it is falling short of God's perfect standard. No one is exempt.
cards.question: When you reflect on your life, in what ways do you recognize your own need before God?

cards.heading: The consequence of sin is death
cards.scriptureText: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
cards.body: Sin carries a serious consequence: death — not just physical death, but spiritual separation from God forever. Yet this verse doesn't end in despair. It pivots to the greatest news: eternal life is offered freely as a gift through Jesus Christ.
cards.question: What does it mean to you that eternal life is a gift, not something you can earn?

cards.heading: God demonstrates His love — Christ died for us
cards.scriptureText: But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
cards.body: God did not wait for us to clean up our lives before sending help. While we were still in our sin — still His enemies — Christ went to the cross for us. This is the depth of God's love: sacrificial, unconditional, and personal.
cards.question: How does it change your view of God to know He loved you before you ever turned to Him?

cards.heading: Confess and believe — and you will be saved
cards.scriptureText: If you declare with your mouth, 'Jesus is Lord,' and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
cards.body: Salvation comes through genuine faith — believing in your heart that Jesus rose from the dead and confessing Him as Lord with your mouth. This is not a mere ritual or formality. It is a wholehearted trust that transforms your life from the inside out.
cards.question: Do you believe in your heart that God raised Jesus from the dead? What would it look like to confess Him as Lord today?

cards.heading: Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved
cards.scriptureText: For, 'Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.'
cards.body: The invitation is open to everyone — no exceptions. No past is too dark, no sin too great. The word 'everyone' leaves no one out. Calling on the Lord means turning to Him in faith, trusting Him alone for your salvation.
cards.question: What is stopping you from calling on the name of the Lord right now?

cards.heading: Nothing can separate us from the love of God
cards.scriptureText: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor demons, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers, neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
cards.body: Once you are in Christ, your salvation is secure. No circumstance, failure, spiritual force, or passage of time can sever you from God's love. This is the assurance and peace that comes with knowing Jesus — a love that holds you forever.
cards.question: How does the promise of God's unbreakable love give you confidence and hope for your life?
